title: Perplexity Teammates AI Agents Arrive on Mac — Behind a $200 Paywall
summary: Perplexity's Teammates AI agents are now on the Mac desktop app — but locked behind the $200/month Max plan. Here's what Teammates do, how the Mac integration works, and how it compares to ChatGPT and Gemini agent offerings.

# Perplexity Teammates AI Agents Arrive on Mac — Behind a $200 Paywall


By OpenTools Team


·


November 15, 2026


Perplexity brought its Teammates AI agents to the Mac desktop app this week, but access requires the $200/month Max plan. The always‑on agents, launched on the web a week earlier, can perform ongoing research, monitoring, and task execution independently.


## What Teammates Actually Do


Perplexity launched Teammates as always-on AI agents on the web in early November 2026, and on November 14 the feature arrived in the Mac desktop app,[AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/perplexity-brings-teammates-agents-to-mac-200-max-plan-only) reported. Unlike standard AI chat assistants that respond to one prompt at a time, Teammates are designed to run independently — monitoring topics, conducting multi-step research, and executing tasks without the user needing to be present.


The agents can search the web autonomously, compile research reports, track developments on specific topics over time, and execute multi-step workflows. Perplexity positions them as "always-on" — you set a task or a monitoring brief, and the agent works in the background, surfacing results when ready. The Mac integration means Teammates can run alongside other desktop workflows without requiring a browser tab to stay open.


## The $200 Gate: Max Plan Only


Access to Teammates on Mac requires the **$200/month Max plan** — Perplexity's top tier. This is not available on the $20/month Pro plan. The Max plan also includes unlimited Pro searches, higher usage limits, and priority access to new features.


[Perplexity](https://perplexity.ai/) confirmed the Max-only access on its pricing page. The pricing puts Perplexity's agent offering at roughly the same level as ChatGPT Pro ($200/month), which also gates agent features behind its top tier. But there's a key difference: ChatGPT Pro's "dots" agents focus on completing purchases and transactions through ChatGPT Wallet, while Perplexity's Teammates focus on research, monitoring, and knowledge work. Different agent philosophies, same price point.


For individual builders and freelancers, the $200/month question is whether always-on research agents deliver enough productivity gain to justify the cost. At approximately $2,400/year, the subscription competes directly with hiring a part-time virtual assistant — and, as[The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/2026/11/perplexity-teammates-mac) noted in its coverage of the web launch, with other[AI agent](https://opentools.ai/tools/ai-agent) subscriptions that builders may already be paying for — and with other AI agent subscriptions that builders may already be paying for.


## Competitive Context: The Agent Pricing War


Perplexity's Teammates enter a rapidly crowding agent market where pricing is becoming the key differentiator. ChatGPT Pro at $200/month includes dots agents with transaction capabilities via ChatGPT Wallet, as[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/13/openai-chatgpt-wallet-dot-purchases.html) detailed.[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) 's Gemini agents are included in Google One AI Premium at $20/month but with more limited autonomy.[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's Claude agents are available through the API with usage-based pricing rather than a subscription model.


Perplexity's advantage is its search-native architecture. Teammates are built on top of Perplexity's real-time web search capabilities, making them better suited for research and monitoring tasks than transaction-oriented agents. The disadvantage is that Perplexity lacks the developer ecosystem that[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) and Anthropic have built — there's no Perplexity equivalent of OpenAI's Commerce Partner Playbook or Anthropic's Model Context Protocol for extending agent capabilities.


## The Mac Desktop Play


Bringing Teammates to the Mac app is a deliberate platform bet. Desktop apps have deeper system access than browser tabs — they can send notifications, run in the background, and maintain persistent connections. For always-on agents that are supposed to work while you're doing other things, the desktop is a more natural home than the browser.


The move also puts Perplexity in direct competition with Apple Intelligence, which is built into macOS at the operating system level and included free with Apple devices. Perplexity's bet is that a specialized, search-native agent is worth $200/month even when a free OS-level AI assistant is available. Whether builders agree remains to be seen.


## What's Missing


[Perplexity's developer docs](https://docs.perplexity.ai/) show no API for Teammates, meaning builders can't integrate the agents into their own workflows or build custom agent behaviors on top of them. There's no equivalent of[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's dots API or[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's tool-use protocol. Teammates are a consumer product, not a platform — at least for now.


The company also hasn't clarified the agent's error-handling behavior. What happens when a Teammate hits a paywalled article during autonomous research? How does the agent handle contradictory sources? What's the fallback behavior when a task exceeds the agent's capability? These are the questions that determine whether always-on agents are genuinely useful or just expensive toys — and Perplexity hasn't answered them publicly yet.


The $200/month price also raises a sustainability question: at that rate, Perplexity would need roughly 500,000 Max subscribers to generate $1.2 billion in annual revenue — a number that would put it in competition with OpenAI's reported $20 billion run rate. The math suggests Max is positioned as a premium tier for power users, not a mass-market product, and Teammates are the feature designed to convert those power users.
